chunks: Al-Saffar, from al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Ghiyath ibn Kallub, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Ja'far, from his father عليهما السلام, that Ali عليه السلام used to say:

Whoever pardons regarding the blood, from among those who have a share in it, then his pardon is valid, the blood-claim is dropped, the indemnity becomes due, and the share of the one who pardoned is lifted from him.

key_terms.الدَّمِ: the blood-claim, meaning the retaliatory claim in a killing case
key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: blood money or indemnity due in place of retaliation
key_terms.ذَوِي سَهْمٍ: those who possess a legal share or entitlement in the matter

ai.seo_question: If one of the heirs in a murder case forgives, is that pardon legally valid and what happens to the blood-claim?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning the heirs or entitled claimants in a blood-case. If one of those who has a recognized share in the claim pardons, that pardon is legally valid, the claim for blood is dropped, and the matter turns to indemnity, with the pardoning party's share excluded.
